cards.question: What is the relationship between AI, Machine Learning, and Deep Learning?
cards.answer: Machine Learning is a broad subset of AI. Deep Learning is an important subset of Machine Learning that uses layered, hierarchical learning — neural networks are a natural way to implement it.

cards.question: What is the relationship between Deep Learning and Neural Networks?
cards.answer: Deep Learning refers to ML methods that use layered, hierarchical learning. Neural networks are a natural practical implementation of Deep Learning — not the other way around.

cards.question: What is the relationship between Machine Learning and Neural Networks?
cards.answer: Neural Networks are one out of many algorithms available for Machine Learning — they are not a replacement for ML as a whole.

cards.question: What is a classification problem in ML?
cards.answer: A problem where the output is a discrete category or label — e.g. determining if a video makes a copyright infringement (yes/no), or identifying if a keyword was spoken in audio.

cards.question: What is a regression problem in ML?
cards.answer: A problem where the output is a continuous numerical value — e.g. predicting the number of views a video will get in its first week, or estimating the age of a speaker from audio.

cards.question: What is a clustering problem in ML?
cards.answer: A problem where the goal is to group similar items together without predefined labels — e.g. grouping students who failed on similar exam questions to suggest tailored practice materials.

cards.question: A program analyzes a lecture video clip and outputs whether it is likely to appear on the final exam. Is this classification or regression?
cards.answer: Classification — the output is a discrete label (relevant / not relevant), not a continuous number.

cards.question: What is Supervised Learning?
cards.answer: Learning from labeled data where each example has an input and a known correct output — e.g. training a license plate recognition model using annotated images of plates.

cards.question: What is Unsupervised Learning?
cards.answer: Learning that finds patterns or structure in data without labels — e.g. grouping songs by recurring lyric themes, or distributing artists across festival shows based on shared fan overlap.

cards.question: What is Reinforcement Learning?
cards.answer: Learning where an agent improves behavior by receiving scores/rewards from its environment — e.g. training a bipedal robot by scoring it on total distance walked in a simulation.

cards.question: What is Self-supervised Learning?
cards.answer: A form of learning where the labels are automatically generated from the data itself — e.g. pretraining a network to predict randomly removed words from messages, without human annotation.

cards.question: What is an advantage of creating your own annotated dataset?
cards.answer: You can use data sampled from your exact final application. If done correctly, there should be no significant difference between your training data and your target data after deployment.

cards.question: What is a disadvantage of creating your own annotated dataset?
cards.answer: It is an expensive and time-consuming process prone to errors. You need safeguards to guarantee the quality of the data collected.

cards.question: Why is data normalization needed?
cards.answer: All of these: many ML models are sensitive to the range of attribute values; it can make learned parameters more explainable; and it allows comparing values that cannot otherwise be compared directly.

cards.question: Why is label encoding needed?
cards.answer: All of these: many ML models can only work with numerical inputs; many can only produce numerical outputs; and encoding allows the model to process categorical data mathematically.

cards.question: Is it a good strategy to merge train/validation/test splits and re-split using cross-validation?
cards.answer: Most likely no. The original splits may be disjoint in subtle domain-specific ways. Randomly re-splitting can destroy this property and lead to poor generalization estimates.

cards.question: A music service wants to create 25 playlists per user based on recurring themes in liked songs' lyrics. What type of learning fits best?
cards.answer: Unsupervised Learning — the goal is to discover recurring thematic clusters in lyrics without predefined labels.

cards.question: A team trains a gesture recognition model using labeled recordings of people drawing specific gestures. What type of learning is this?
cards.answer: Supervised Learning — each gesture recording is paired with a known label indicating which gesture was drawn.
